text:
Washington got its decisive goal from a line that did nearly all the work. Jordan Kyrou scored twice, Dylan Strome had three assists, and Jack St. Ivany added two, and all three were on the ice for both of Kyrou's goals. St. Ivany has his own history with this opponent: the Flyers drafted him 112th overall in 2018, and he spent his first years in their system before turning up in Washington's lineup.

The 5-2 final fits how the game was played. By our numbers, WSH deserved to win about 67% of the time, meaning two-thirds of simulated replays of every shot ended in a Capitals win. Expected goals, our measure of chance quality, was 4.53 to 2.45 for WSH, and the Capitals led it in every period, including a 1.49 to 0.68 first. Shot attempts were nearly even (62 to 61), so the gap came from where the shots came from. Alex Tuch had five shots on goal and scored twice, the second into an empty net late. Alex Ovechkin's 37% look in the first period, the best chance that didn't go in, was stopped by Joseph Woll.

PHI never fully faded. Sean Couturier tipped in a goal in the second, and Matvei Michkov cut it to 3-2 on a power play in the third, but Kyrou answered about three minutes later. Logan Thompson stopped 23 of 25 shots, slightly better than the chances he faced, while Woll allowed four goals on 3.45 expected. We have no streak or record information for either team, so the one thing we can say is that WSH took this game on its merits.
